acceptance.given: Package A implementation and test changes are prepared within the repository scope defined by the frozen requirements.

oracle.expected: The inspected change manifest contains no paths under PhaseA.Platform/**, PhaseA.Platform.Tests/**, runtime/**, live metadata, hosted workspaces, Phase authentication or authorization, or the Runner.
forbidden: Any changed path matches PhaseA.Platform/** or PhaseA.Platform.Tests/**.
Any changed path matches runtime/**, live metadata, or hosted workspace paths.
Any changed path modifies Phase authentication/authorization or the Runner.
oracle.observable: A repository change-manifest or equivalent artifact is evaluated during the scope-boundary check and records the changed paths.

acceptance.then: The scope-boundary check reports whether any changed Package A path enters a named Phase or runtime boundary.
acceptance.when: During acceptance validation, inspect the repository change manifest against each forbidden scope prefix and component boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A test selector evaluates the Package A change manifest and fails with an assertion identifying any forbidden Phase, runtime, metadata, workspace, authentication/authorization, or Runner path.

affected_subjects: Package A Phase and runtime scope boundary
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add Package A authoring-standard validation while enforcing a repository change boundary that excludes all named Phase, runtime, live-state, authentication/authorization, and Runner areas.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Remove or revert only Package A files and preserve all Phase service, runtime, live metadata, workspace, authentication/authorization, and Runner state.

slice_hint.state_transition: Package A scope moves from an unmodified boundary declaration to a validated change set whose paths are checked against forbidden Phase and runtime boundaries.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The scope-boundary validation completes and records zero changed paths in every forbidden boundary; any violation causes failure.
